title: AI, ML, and Data Engineering InfoQ Trends Report 2026
gist: InfoQ's AI/ML trends podcast panel (Huyen, Dominguez, Luu, Casals) sees model value shifting to system design, inference and evals exploding, agents becoming organization-wide while junior hiring shrinks, and energy and US-China infrastructure competition as 2027 constraints.

insights.claim: Frontier-model headlines are shifting from which model is best to which combination fits a workload's capability, latency, data boundary and cost, making it a system design question.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: Multi-model routing and orchestration layers gain value as models commoditize.
insights.locator: Arthur Casals: Yes, I think in general

insights.claim: New model releases follow a pattern of a big top-benchmark model followed within weeks by a cheaper, smaller one only 1-2% worse via distillation, sparse mixture of experts and quantization; 1-2 bit models now appear versus 4-bit seeming crazy a few years ago.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: Rapid cost-per-capability deflation pressures frontier pricing.
insights.locator: Another trend I see from models

insights.claim: Enterprise fine-tuning is rare and concentrated in healthcare and finance, remains more craft than process and is costly, so adoption is unclear.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: Fine-tuning demand may be narrower than hype suggests.
insights.locator: There was a lot of interest in doing fine-tuning

insights.claim: Inference exploded in 2026 as vLLM and SGLang plus capable open-weight models let firms self-host, particularly financial firms with PII and those cutting coding costs.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: Self-hosted inference and neocloud providers benefit; hardware still predominantly Nvidia with AMD coming online.
insights.locator: Totally. The inference topics

insights.claim: Older-generation chips become nearly free to run and smaller models fit them, while upstart chipmakers can compete at lower-tier architectures rather than Nvidia's flagship; Cerebras is named as an interesting player.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: Possible niche for older and alternative silicon in inference.
insights.locator: I'm curious because I think this is a trend

insights.claim: TypeSafe AI's Jev is a System One model built for software consumers that is extremely fast and unlocks new use cases, including UI generation.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: Fast deterministic decision models could cut agent costs.
insights.locator: I've been watching a lot of videos on this

insights.claim: Agents are moving from personal to team to whole-organization scope and from interface to execution layer, with software development the clearest case via Claude, Codex, Cursor and Replit.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: Agent adoption is shifting spend toward governance, permissions and observability.
insights.locator: AI agents are probably one of the biggest trends

insights.claim: Coding agents need operational design with authority levels, permissions and auditing, and tools should be written for software agents rather than for humans.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: Agent-native tooling is an opening for infrastructure vendors.
insights.locator: First, we need to separate coding assistants

insights.claim: Agent SDKs from LangChain, Anthropic and OpenAI are expanding into harness engineering, including memory, code execution and hosted runtimes.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: Platform bundling of agent runtimes.
insights.locator: One thing I want to add to discussions of agent

insights.claim: Panelists say they have stopped hiring junior and front-end developers and hire people who can specify systems and use AI; developers become agent orchestrators, raising the question of how to train new hires.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: Anecdotal evidence of shrinking entry-level engineering demand.
insights.locator: For example, in my experience right now we stop hiring junior developers

insights.claim: Multi-agent systems face missing standards: messaging protocols exist but no standard architecture, state or environment description, so interoperability is hard.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: Interoperability gaps limit cross-vendor agent ecosystems.
insights.locator: One of the problems of the multi-agent systems area

insights.claim: Chip Huyen's own multi-agent experiment failed when agents forwarded tasks to each other and none did the work.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: Naive agent-to-agent messaging can loop; scope awareness required.
insights.locator: So what happened after that is that my task

insights.claim: Daniel Dominguez expects multi-provider AI usage like multi-cloud rather than single-vendor lock-in.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: Argues against winner-take-all among model providers for enterprises.
insights.locator: Yes. In my opinion, I think it's going to happen

insights.claim: Context pollution is the biggest context problem: larger windows do not help if systems cannot tell current from stale or adversarial material.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: Memory management and retrieval quality outweigh window size.
insights.locator: Context pollution is actually the biggest problem

insights.claim: 2026 is the year of evaluations: companies build evaluation harnesses as go/no-go gates for customer-facing agents, scoring completion, cost, time, interventions and safety across model, tool, context and environment.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: Eval tooling is a durable category as agents reach production.
insights.locator: This is a very important topic for companies

insights.claim: Physical AI differs from software agents because errors have physical consequences, and robotics is adopting multimodal foundation models combining vision, language and action.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: Reliability and simulation tooling for robots.
insights.locator: Basically it's saying

insights.claim: Robot learning cannot backtrack like LLM training, and companies like Physical Intelligence, Generalist, Sunday and Skild AI are betting on different data strategies including teleoperation, video and haptic gloves.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: Data approach is the key uncertainty for robot scaling.
insights.locator: One big difference between robotics, models, and LLMs

insights.claim: AI private investment has grown exponentially while exits via acquisitions and IPOs are essentially nil, while company sizes shrink and winner-take-all attention dominates.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: Capital-in without capital-out is a classic late-cycle risk marker.
insights.locator: So it's going absolutely crazy

insights.claim: Chip Huyen wants US robot companies shipping to buyers and flags that delayed OpenAI and Anthropic IPOs could impact market and funding depending on outcome.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: IPO reception is a key sentiment test for AI funding.
insights.locator: I really want to see US robot companies

insights.claim: Daniel Dominguez predicts energy and electricity access, capacity and cooling will become the biggest AI growth constraint, with infrastructure possibly moving to space and US-China competition becoming a technological Cold War over manufacturing, energy, data centers, open models and supply chains.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: Favors power, grid and non-model infrastructure plays and geopolitics sensitivity.
insights.quote: some of the biggest AI stories may actually happen outside the models themselves
insights.locator: I think we're going to start seeing limitations on AI

insights.claim: Hien Luu predicts every agent will incorporate a Jev-style model and communication will increasingly be agent to agent.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: Directional bet on System One models.
insights.locator: Just two things

insights.claim: Arthur Casals predicts successful deployments will use smaller specialized agents on well-defined tasks, with differentiation in trusted data, permissions, visibility and task-level ROI.
insights.speaker: Chip Huyen
insights.so_what: ROI per task, not tokens, becomes the metric.
insights.locator: I'll circle back to what I said at the beginning
